data.title: Anthropic unifies Claude Chat and Cowork for enterprise plans
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) has unified Claude Chat and Cowork for enterprise plan subscribers that can be used on web, desktop and mobile devices.

"The new unified Claude experience brings chat and Cowork together on web, desktop, and mobile," Anthropic posted today on its Claude Support webpage. "Members no longer choose between chat and Cowork before they start. Every conversation starts as a chat, and when a task needs to run code or work with files, Claude continues the same conversation in an isolated cloud sandbox managed by Anthropic, then returns the finished work for review."

The new unified experience was made generally available today but currently requires an administrator to turn it on. Anthropic said the unified experience will be turned on by default beginning Nov. 16.

Iovance sees long-term response for Amtagvi in first-line melanoma
data.description:
• An analysis of phase 2 data found that a one-time treatment of Iovance Biotherapeutics' (IOVA) Amtagvi (lifileucel) combined with Merck's (MRK) Keytruda (pembrolizumab) led to a 62.5% objective response rate and a 29.2% complete response rate after a median follow-up of 50.9 months as a frontline treatment for advanced melanoma.
  • Median overall survival, however, was not reached at the timepoint.
  • The analysis of the IOV-COM-202 trial also found that median progression-free survival was 19.8 months and the disease control rate was 83.3%.
  • Amtagvi, a polyclonal tumor infiltrating lymphocyte ("TIL") cellular immunotherapy, was granted accelerated approval in 2024 for individuals with unresectable or metastatic melanoma who failed on a PD-1 inhibitor.
  • Iovance has also started enrollment in TILVANCE-301, a phase 3 study examining Amtagvi in combination with Keytruda compared with Keytruda alone in patients with untreated, unresectable, or metastatic melanoma.

Skydance's size creates synergy opportunities but also risks from cord-cutting, bundling -- JP Morgan
data.description:
With the merger of Paramount Skydance with Warner Bros. Discovery complete and shares off restriction, J.P. Morgan gives the newly formed Skydance (SKYD) a Neutral rating and $9 price target ($15 upside from Thursday’s close), weighing the opportunities created by such a large media company against the challenges in maintaining subscribers and the potential for a downturn in the advertising market.

A company of this size, which is larger by revenue than Netflix (NFLX) and Disney ex-parks (DIS), “creates opportunities to improve content monetization, cross-sell streaming services, and remove duplicated costs,” said analyst David Karnovsky. But with linear as the key earnings contributor and 6.1x 2026e net leverage, Skydance (SKYD) has “little room for execution missteps or challenges outside the company’s control.”

Karnovsky believes Skydance (SKYD) can achieve its synergy goal but respects investor skepticism that the company can reach its EBITDA and free cash flow targets.

“We believe the market will need to see evidence that the integration is improving cash generation before becoming more constructive,” Karnovsky notes.

The movie business looks promising with a 2027-2028 pipeline that includes The Batman Part II, The Hunt for Gollum, Sonic 4, Man of Tomorrow, and Minecraft, while Karnovsky views the 30-32 film mandate as manageable.

“But the growth plan requires a wide-release output and cadence that only Universal has successfully executed since 2021,”

In streaming, ad-free pricing premiums and bundling are the “real levers” for earnings growth. However, the Disney+ and Hulu bundle underscores the challenges of combining platforms. Moreover, subscriber growth must occur at the same time Netflix (NFLX) and Disney (DIS) are increasing spending on content and acquisition costs.

Since the merger was completed on October 6, shares of Skydance (SKYD) have been down 18%, with the bulk of the loss occurring after the company issued 470M warrants.

data.title: Trump prepares tariff relief on Canada ahead of midterms - report
data.description:
The Trump administration is preparing to eliminate 50% tariffs on select Canadian agricultural and forestry imports in a bid to shield Sen. Susan Collins (R., Maine) and other border-state Republicans ahead of the midterm elections, according to a media report published Friday.

The forthcoming presidential proclamation could be signed as early as Friday, although the scope and timing could change, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Still, the administration may offset the relief by levying new duties on other Canadian goods, the WSJ noted.

The cross-border dispute started in late August, when the White House invoked Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act—commonly known as Smoot-Hawley—to penalize Canadian imports, prompting retaliatory measures from Ottawa and threats of further auto tariffs.

The planned exemptions are aimed mainly at boosting Collins, who is locked in a neck-and-neck race against Democrat Troy Jackson. Jackson has made the trade war a central campaign theme in Maine, where border commerce is key.

The prospective tariff overhaul comes amid mounting pushback, with a New Jersey food importer filing a lawsuit this week challenging the legality of using Smoot-Hawley powers for the levies.

Prediction market Kalshi has a 67% chance of a Democratic sweep of Congress in the midterms, pricing unified Democratic control well ahead of divided government or a Republican sweep.

A White House official dismissed advance reports of tariff adjustments as speculation, while the U.S. Trade Representative’s office declined to comment, the Journal said.

data.title: MSC Industrial wins two brokerage upgrades after post-earnings plunge
data.description:
MSC Industrial Direct (MSM) rose 2.8% in Friday's trading after scoring upgrades from analysts at Jefferies and Stephens following the stock's 15% post-earnings plunge in the previous session that showed FQ4 net income and operating margin declining Y/Y to $47.9M and 6.7%, respectively.

Jefferies analyst Stephen Volkmann upgraded MSC (MSM) to Buy from Hold with a $135 price target, edged up from $130, citing improving fundamentals and expected acceleration in volume growth momentum in 2027 alongside continued productivity improvement.

MSC's (MSM) profit margins should continue to expand at 20%-30% incrementals given low variable costs, with headcount productivity providing a path toward mid-teens EBIT margins compared to ~10% currently, Volkmann wrote.

Stephens analyst Tommy Moll noted the shares now sit below his previous $113 bear-case scenario, prompting him to upgrade to Overweight from Equal Weight, also with a $135 PT.

MSC (MSM) had climbed 55% YTD leading into the earnings report, but Moll said elevated buyside expectations and a down day in the broader market prompted the stock's 15% slide, but future potential positive catalysts include inflation-driven margin tailwinds and a manufacturing volume-based recovery, whether driven by the end market or the company's internal initiatives.
